title: Microlaunch coordination notebook (LLM experiments)
content:
Purpose: quick, low-friction coordination guide for multi-team microlaunches of LLM-driven features. This is intentionally lightweight — a living notebook for planning, execution, and fast deconfliction across product, infra, SRE, safety, and CS.

Context and intent:
- We run frequent small-scope LLM experiments (feature pilots, rerank tweaks, prompt variants). The goal here is to reduce friction for multi-team launches while keeping safety and observability tight.
- These notes came from a cross-functional sync (2025-02-11) and in-the-field lessons from two pilot weekends.

High-level microlaunch pattern (4 stages):
1) Scope + quick risk triage (T-7 to T-2 days)
   - Define the minimal surface (API route, user cohort, variant). Keep the initial cohort <= 0.5% of traffic when possible.
   - Quick triage checklist: does the change affect prompting, model selection, or routing? Any data exfil risk? Must we use private deployment or dedicated capacity?
   - Owners assigned: product owner, infra lead, safety reviewer, observability steward, CS contact.

2) Preflight (T-2 to T) — rehearsal and canaries
   - Deploy variant to a staging slice with synthetic traffic and recorded real traffic replays. Run canary smoke tests: latency P50/P95, 99th-percentile CPU/GPU per-infer, error-rate, memory.
   - Safety quick checks: automated classifier run on 1k prompt/responses, manual review of 50 edge cases, fuzzing with adversarial prompts.
   - Gate: if any safety classifier hit rate > 2% or manual review shows unacceptable failure modes -> block.

3) Microlaunch activation (T+0 through T+48h)
   - Start with a tiny live cohort (0.1% -> 0.5%) for 4–12 hours. Observe signals and hold on manual gate if signals spike.
   - Primary signals to watch (live telemetry):
     * Latency p50/p95/p99 (tokens/sec, end-to-end API latency)
     * Error rate (5xxs, model runtime errors)
     * Token cost delta and GPU utilization (cost burn rate)
     * Business KPIs upstream (CTR, completion rate, conversion) — watch relative delta vs baseline
     * Safety signals: classifier flags (toxicity, PII leakage), content-moderation hits, user reports
     * Semantic quality indicators: automatic BLEU-like proxies where applicable, rerank precision/CTR lift for rerankers
   - Communication: #microlaunch (Slack) channel created, short cadence updates from steward every 2 hours during first day.

4) Ramp / closeout (T+48h onward)
   - If signals stable and within budgets for 48h, expand increments: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> broader. Each step hold 6–12h for rapid checks.
   - If any critical signal breaches pre-agreed thresholds -> immediate rollback path (see rollback matrix below).
   - Post-launch: write a short 1-pager with observed telemetry, surprises, and follow-ups. Tag relevant PRs and add to experiment ledger.

Owner and role cheat-sheet (minimal):
- Product owner: hypothesis, target cohort, success metric, stakeholders.
- Infra lead: capacity plan, autoscaling knobs, cost limit guardrails.
- Observability steward: dashboards set up 24h prior, alert thresholds configured, synthetic probes.
- Safety reviewer: run checks and be on-call during activation window.
- CS contact: monitor feedback channels and handle escalations.
- Oncall engineer: runbook contact for rollbacks and emergency mitigation.

Quick guardrails and thresholds (configurable per experiment):
- Latency: p95 increase > 30% relative to baseline -> investigate; > 50% -> pause expansion.
- Error rate: absolute 5xx rate > 0.5% -> pause; > 1% -> rollback.
- Safety classifier hits: > 1.5% flagged content in rolling 1000 -> hold; > 3% -> rollback.
- Cost: projected token/GPU spend > allocated budget for 72h -> throttle or switch to smaller model.

Rollback matrix (fast actions):
- Minor degradation (latency spike under 50%, small classifier uptick): throttle traffic, enable fallbacks, notify stakeholders.
- Major degradation (safety classifier > 3% or sustained error rate > 1%): immediate toggle off variant at edge, route to baseline model, page oncall.
- Emergency (unknown catastrophic behavior, severe user harm): full halt of experiment, incident creation, coordinate with legal and comms.

Pre-launch checklist (quick):
- [ ] Hypothesis documented (metric + expected direction)
- [ ] Owner + 2 backups named
- [ ] Dashboards + alerts created and smoke-tested
- [ ] Safety checks run and signed off by reviewer
- [ ] Capacity plan + cost cap configured
- [ ] Comms plan + Slack channel ready

During-launch checklist (first 48h):
- [ ] Steward posts status every 2–4 hours for day 1, every 6–12 hours afterward
- [ ] Observability steward validates synthetic probe health each check-in
- [ ] Safety reviewer samples latest 100 responses for drift
- [ ] CS monitors user inbox/tickets for anomalies

Post-launch quick retro template (to paste):
- What did we expect? (hypothesis)
- What happened (top-line telemetry)?
- Where did we deviate (bugs, infra, model quality)?
- Immediate follow-ups (owners + ETA)
- Longer-term learnings

Operational notes and shortcuts (field tricks learned):
- Keep the first slice ALWAYS read-only for users where possible — use an opt-in cohort. That reduces exposure and simplifies rollback.
- Have a fast model-substitution plan: if the model instance misbehaves, swap to smaller/safer variant instead of full rollback to baseline to preserve feature continuity.
- Use synthetic traffic generators that mimic token length distribution — token-cost surprises bite hard.
- If a safety classifier is noisy, prefer short manual review bursts sampling edge cases rather than pausing the whole experiment while tweaking classifier thresholds.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we standardize microlaunch increments (0.1/0.5/2/10) or keep flexible per experiment? (action: product-led decision).
- Need a lightweight templated dashboard that auto-populates with model variant metadata + cost burn rate (action: observability team ticket ENG-2410).
- Can we build an automated quick-sanity runner that ensembles safety classifiers to reduce manual review burden? (action: safety + applied-ml explore PoC).

Next steps (short):
1) Ship this notebook to Confluence as "Microlaunch lightweight playbook" and link from new-experiment template.
2) Obs team to prototype the autoset dashboard (ENG-2410).
3) Schedule a 1-hour brown-bag to align teams on thresholds and escalation flow (target: week of 2025-03-10).

Notes to self: keep this file short and keep one-liners for oncall. If we need more rigor, spin a full playbook with gating matrices and automation scripts. For now: low friction + high observability.

Scratchpad (quick links):
- Incident runbook: confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Incident+Playbook
- Experiment ledger (sheet): https://sheets.redwood.ai/experiments-ledger
- Slack channels: #microlaunch, #prod-oncall, #model-safety

End of notebook.
